Built · 26 August 2026

The project tables, as built

These are screenshots of the real platform, not a drawing. Every table below came out of the built file a minute ago, at the width a pane actually has, in whichever theme you are reading this in. Finance › FIN01, all three panes.

One table, one row shape. A deliverable is an outcome whose direction is = and whose target is Y/N — written by the platform, shown quietly, because a value nobody can change should not look like a field. The Type column says which kind a row is.

The due date is off the deliverable-and-outcome tables and off the upload template, as you asked. It is not deleted: where a plan carries one it still decides whether a row is asked for this cycle and whether it is late — that reading moved under the row’s name rather than disappearing. Milestones keep their column, now as a month and a year: July 2026.

One thing I got wrong the first time, and fixed before writing this. You said a row should be gated on its due date “however they can report on it exceptional”. The build did the opposite: a row that was not due had its dropdown replaced by the words “Not asked”, so the one thing you asked for was the one thing the pane refused. Worse, on Performance a row somebody had delivered early read as a dash while its 100% went on counting toward the score — the screen disagreeing with the number beside it.

Not due is a label now, not a lock. The control is always there; the words sit where the reading would be and step aside the moment there is one. You can see it on Reporting below: row 6 is not due, dimmed, and still has a live box; row 4 was delivered early and now reads plainly.

Capability › Projects — the plan pane

Five columns and every cell answered. Rows 1–4 are deliverables: = and Y/N are written in quietly. Rows 5 and 6 are outcomes and carry their own direction and target. The milestone table keeps Name, Description, Owner and Due date — the four fields you specified, with the date now reading March 2026.

Capability › Performance — the scoreboard

Status holds the word for a deliverable and the figure for an outcome; % holds the number the score is built from, for both, so the score column runs down one edge. Row 3 is overdue and says so under its name — that reading used to live in the due-date cell and moved rather than disappeared. Row 4 was delivered early: it is due December, it reads 100%, and it counts. Row 6 is not due and nothing has been said about it: dimmed, and marked as such.

Capability › Reporting — where the figures are entered

A deliverable picks a status and the per-cent follows — 100 for Delivered, 0 for Not started, a box only for In progress, which is the whole of “in progress requires a per-cent of completion”. An outcome types a figure and its per-cent is computed against the target. Row 6 is the fix: not due, dimmed, marked Not due — and the box is live, so it can be reported early. The tally reads what you owe this cycle, not everything in the plan.

What is behind it

  • Nobody’s score moved, and it is asserted rather than promised: the check strips every per-cent and compares Execution’s old formula against the new one across all eight capabilities. Identical, eight times.
  • The new rule is asserted from the failing side. I put the old behaviour back three times — the milestone lock, the Performance dash, the status pill — and the check went red for each. The first version of it stayed green on a reverted build, because FIN01 has no not-due milestone at all, so the check now makes the four cases rather than hoping the demo carries them.
  • A workbook downloaded before today still uploads. Its Kind column is read and ignored; its deliverables simply have no date, which is now true of all of them.
  • The full sweep is clean — every page as every viewer, no console errors.

What I would still put in front of you

  • The outcome sheet keeps its date column, deliberately. Taking it out too would stop a plan ever saying when an outcome is measured, and “not asked until Q4” has been in the product since the capability model existed. Say the word if you want it gone as well.
  • The database round trip is not run. Migration 023 needs a live Postgres, which this session does not have. I would want that green before this reaches production.
  • Reporting is seven columns now the date has gone. Still the widest table in the product, on the page somebody fills in under time pressure. The lever to make it six is reading the status out of the per-cent instead of asking both — on the table if you want it.
  • The same not-due lock is still on a unit’s tactics table, which I have not touched because you did not ask about it. It is the same fault and the same one-line shape of fix. Yours to say.
  • Still unfixed from before: a project’s drag handles are bound to nothing — sortAttr() is defined and applied to neither table. What a drop between a deliverable and an outcome should mean is a decision, not a bug fix.
